question: Our medical device plant in Indiana is a major source of HAP. On the breathing-circuit assembly lines we bond polymer sub-assemblies by applying methylene chloride so the plastic softens and fuses as the solvent evaporates; nothing with solids is applied and no dry film is left behind. We are adding six more of these lines. Does the NESHAP for surface coating of plastic parts cover this solvent welding step?
notes: Not subject to PPPP. MeCl applied to bond two surfaces is an 'adhesive' and therefore a coating under 63.4581, but with no coating solids the 63.4490 emission limit (lb HAP per lb solids) cannot be determined, so the rule is not applied to the solvent welding lines. Letter 2020-06-16, Region 5.

question: We are proposing a copper recovery plant in North Carolina permitted as a synthetic minor (area source) for HAP. Scrap tubing, wire, radiators and brass casings are sorted to at least 90 percent copper, melted in a natural-gas-fired tilting anode furnace with silica and lime flux, oxidized with air, reduced with natural gas and cast into 99.7 percent copper anodes that are shipped off site for refining. There is no sweating or burning of insulation. Is this facility a secondary copper smelter under the area source NESHAP?
notes: Subject to FFFFFF. The anode furnace is a pyrometallurgical purification process that produces anode copper from scrap, meeting the 63.11158 definition of secondary copper smelter; a new area source is covered by 63.11153(a)-(b). Letter 2020-08-14, Region 4.

question: We run a small perchloroethylene dry cleaning shop in Michigan. There is an apartment above the shop that is currently unoccupied, and the machine is often idle because the location is mainly a pick-up and drop-off store. Does the requirement to eliminate perc emissions from dry cleaning systems located in a building with a residence after December 21, 2020 apply to us?
notes: Yes. A co-located residence, occupied or not, makes this a co-residential source; the December 21, 2020 sunset on PCE emissions in 63.322(o)(5)(i) applies as long as the PCE machine stays in the building, whether or not it is currently operating. Letter 2020-08-06, Region 5.

question: Our Massachusetts plant is an area source of HAP and makes modular power supplies and power conversion components for aerospace, defense and computing customers. We are classified under SIC 3679 (electronic components, not elsewhere classified) and NAICS 335999. Are we covered by the area source NESHAP for metal fabrication and finishing?
notes: Not subject to XXXXXX. Applicability under 63.11514(a) turns on being primarily engaged in one of nine source categories; EPA's Q&A chart pairs NAICS 335999 with SIC 3699, not SIC 3679, so the facility is outside the rule. Letter 2020-04-16, Region 1.

question: Our Wyoming trona (soda ash) plant is a major source of HAP. In the caustic recovery loop we run a lime slaker and a natural-gas-fired lime kiln that calcines calcium carbonate lime mud back into quicklime for reuse in the process; we do not process limestone and do not sell lime. Does the NESHAP for lime manufacturing plants apply to our kiln?
notes: Subject to AAAAA. Calcining calcareous lime mud into calcium oxide meets the 63.7143 definition of lime manufacturing plant; the rule exempts pulp mills, beet sugar plants and water-softening sludge but not similar chemical recovery at a soda ash plant, and does not require the lime to be sold. Letter 2021-01-15, Region 8.

question: At our gas plant in Utah, an area source of HAP, we operate three existing 800 hp four-stroke lean-burn natural gas engines that have met the geographic criteria for a remote location since October 2013. We never sent the state a notification of remote status. Can we meet the work practice standards for remote engines instead of doing performance tests?
notes: Yes. No notification of remote status is required for existing non-emergency 4SLB/4SRB SI engines over 500 HP at area sources, but the owner must evaluate remote status every 12 months and keep records under 63.6603(f); 'conditional' approval is for the delegated state (Utah DAQ). Letter 2021-02-11, Region 8.

question: Our nuclear power station in Michigan is an area source of HAP. An audit found two 500-gallon gasoline tanks and one 500-gallon diesel tank used only to fuel company vehicles; none of them are in our operating permit. Are these tanks covered by the area source NESHAP for gasoline dispensing facilities?
notes: The two gasoline tanks are subject to CCCCCC (a gasoline dispensing facility at an area source dispensing into motor vehicles); the diesel tank is not, because diesel is not 'gasoline' under 63.11132. Letter 2021-02-02, Region 5.

question: At our Portland cement plant in Tennessee we divert kiln exhaust to dry pulverized coal in the coal mill, which exhausts through its own stack. We believe the coal mill falls only under the cement NESHAP and not under the NSPS for coal preparation plants. Which particulate limits and compliance demonstrations apply to the coal mill stack?
notes: Both apply. The coal mill is a thermal dryer under NSPS Subpart Y and also part of the LLL affected source; coal mill PM must be tested annually and combined with the kiln stack PM per 63.1349 and 63.1350. Letter 2021-04-30, Region 4.

question: Our Missouri plant recovers aluminum from coated scrap by heating it in delamination chambers to burn off paint and plastic, then grinds it into aluminum granules. We do not melt aluminum and our customers tell us they do not melt the granules either. Does the secondary aluminum NESHAP apply to the delamination units?
notes: Subject to RRR. The delamination chambers meet the 63.1503 definition of scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln; since the 2015 rule revisions applicability no longer depends on whether the recovered aluminum is later melted. Letter 2022-03-25, Region 7.

question: We operate a vehicle service and body repair center in Denver, an area source, where we spray apply refinish coatings to cars. None of the coatings we spray contain the target metal HAP (chromium, lead, manganese, nickel or cadmium) and we can certify that. We occasionally use methylene chloride paint stripper. Can we be exempted from the area source auto body coating requirements?
notes: Exemption granted under 63.11170(a)(2) for the spray coating activities based on the certification that no target HAP coatings are sprayed; paint stripping with methylene chloride remains subject. If target HAP coatings are ever used, submit the initial notification under 63.11175 and comply. Letter 2020-12-14, Region 8.

question: We are a contract coating shop in Wisconsin, an area source, coating metal parts for other manufacturers. One line (a polyurea line) spray applies a coating that contains none of the target HAP metals, while other lines do use them. Is that polyurea line subject to the area source surface coating NESHAP?
notes: Not subject, line by line: for miscellaneous surface coating (unlike motor vehicle coating) the rule applies only to operations that spray apply target-HAP coatings, so line 3 is outside the rule as long as it uses no target HAP coating. Letter 2021-02-16, Region 5.

question: We run a lean premix gas-fired combustion turbine at a natural gas compressor station in Ohio, a major source of HAP. The unit was built after 2003 and has no oxidation catalyst. We want to show compliance with the formaldehyde limit by monitoring gas producer turbine speed and inlet air temperature instead of installing a catalyst. Is that allowed and what must we submit?
notes: Petition approved. A turbine without an oxidation catalyst must petition under 63.6120(e)-(f) for operating limitations; %NGP and inlet air temperature were accepted as operating limits within ranges, to be continuously monitored under 63.6125(b). Letter 2023-05-23, Region 5.

question: Our Connecticut marine railway used to build barges but since 2011 only repairs them: dry abrasive blasting, welding and spray coating of steel hulls, staying under 3,000 gallons a year of coatings and solvents as an area source. We are now classified as ship building and repairing (SIC 3731, NAICS 336611). Does the area source NESHAP for metal fabrication and finishing still apply?
notes: Not subject. Ship building and repairing is not one of the nine source categories in 63.11514(a) and the SIC/NAICS pair is not in EPA's Q&A table; the earlier fabricated structural metal classification no longer describes the facility. Letter 2023-04-10, Region 1.

question: Our Ohio facility, an area source, assembles and repairs progressive cavity pumps (SIC 3561) from components bought elsewhere. We do some spot welding, dry machining, dry grinding, abrasive blasting and spray painting, but fewer than half of the pumps go through those finishing steps. Are we 'primarily engaged' in a covered metal fabrication and finishing category?
notes: Subject to XXXXXX. Pump manufacturing is in the Industrial Machinery and Equipment Finishing Operations category; 'primarily engaged' under 63.11522 is judged by the facility's production of listed products (pumps), not by the share of pumps that receive finishing operations. Letter 2024-01-25, Region 5.

question: At our beryllium products plant in Ohio we use two diesel engines mounted on portable vacuum units that are moved around the site to clean up beryllium-containing material. Are these engines stationary engines subject to the RICE NESHAP?
notes: Not subject to ZZZZ. Engines on portable, transportable equipment meet the nonroad engine definition in 40 CFR 1068.30 and so are not stationary RICE under 63.6675, provided they do not stay at one location more than 12 consecutive months. Letter 2023-05-31, Region 5.

question: Our Indiana plant tests heavy-duty clutches. Seven diesel truck engines of 335 to 600 hp, supplied by engine manufacturers, sit in dynamometer test cells for years and drive the clutch under test through a straight shaft. We think the engine test cell exemptions in the engine rules cover us. Are these engines exempt from the stationary engine NESHAP?
notes: Subject to ZZZZ (and NSPS IIII). Engines kept in test cells beyond 12 months are stationary RICE; the test cell/stand exception covers engines being tested, not engines used as a power source to test other components such as clutches. Letter 2023-09-07, Region 5.

question: Our Michigan power plant has one electric generating boiler permitted for natural gas and fuel oil. Oil is burned only during startup: well under 10 percent of heat input on a three-year average and under 15 percent in any single year. Is this unit covered by the utility mercury and air toxics rule or by the major source boiler MACT?
notes: Exempt from both. With oil below the 10 percent / 15 percent thresholds the unit is not an oil-fired EGU under 63.10042, so UUUUU does not apply; as a natural gas-fired EGU it is excluded from DDDDD by 63.7491(a). Letter 2023-10-24, Region 5.

question: At our Michigan chemical site, a major source of HAP, we make a 2,4-D phenoxy herbicide active ingredient. We want to add a distillation column to strip water from a purchased raw material (70 to 80 percent purity) so it feeds the herbicide unit at 99 percent purity; the raw material is stored in existing tanks in a neighboring building. Which organic chemical NESHAP would the new distillation process fall under?
notes: Subject to NSPS VVa and to either MMM (pesticide active ingredient production) or FFFF (MON); not subject to the HON (F and G) because the distillation serves a pesticide process rather than a SOCMI unit. Letter 2023-12-12, Region 5.

question: We are building a lithium-ion battery cell plant in Michigan that will be an area source of HAP. The cathode line mixes nickel-containing active material, binder and NMP solvent into a slurry that is coated onto foil and dried. Which area source NESHAP applies to the cathode slurry mixing process?
notes: Not VVVVVV (chemical manufacturing area sources). The cathode mixing line is 'paint and allied product manufacturing' under 63.11607 because the slurry is a coating that leaves a dried film and the nickel makes it a HAP-containing material, so CCCCCCC applies. Letter 2020-04-08, Region 5.

question: Our Alabama plant makes glass frit (NAICS 3255) by melting nickel-containing raw materials and quenching the melt into frit used in ceramic glazes and coatings; we are an area source. Between the chemical preparations rule, the paints and allied products rule and the chemical manufacturing area source rule, which one covers frit production?
notes: CCCCCCC applies: NAICS 3255 products intended to leave a dried film on a substrate, and nickel above 0.1 percent makes the material HAP-containing. BBBBBBB does not apply (chemical preparations are NAICS 325998) and VVVVVV does not because 63.11494 excludes sources subject to CCCCCCC. Letter 2020-04-22, Region 4.

question: At our secondary aluminum plant in Ohio we want to install a thermal chip dryer running at about 660 degrees F to drive water off shredded aluminum that carries some paint before the shreds go to the melting furnace. We believe that temperature is too low to form hydrocarbons or dioxins. Would the dryer be an affected source under the secondary aluminum NESHAP?
notes: Yes. Drying painted aluminum shreds is what a 'scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln' does under 63.1503, and the company did not show that 660 degrees F assures no HAP emissions; while processing painted scrap the dryer must meet the major source requirements for that unit. Letter 2020-03-24, Region 5.

question: Two residual-oil-fired utility boilers at our New Hampshire station are sometimes fired only to make auxiliary steam, for example to heat the on-site fuel oil tanks, without generating electricity. Can we treat that operation as startup under the utility mercury and air toxics rule so the startup work practices apply instead of the emission limits?
notes: No. Under the 63.10042 definition, startup ends when steam is generated for any purpose, including auxiliary steam to heat oil tanks, so the units are not in startup while producing auxiliary steam. Letter 2020-01-28, Region 1.

question: Unit 1 at our Connecticut power station is a 4,286 MMBtu per hour steam boiler that burns No. 2 and No. 4 fuel oil as its main fuel with only a small amount of natural gas, and it runs at a low annual capacity factor. Does it qualify as a limited-use liquid oil-fired unit under the utility mercury and air toxics rule?
notes: Yes. Oil is the primary fuel so the unit is an oil-fired EGU under 63.10042, and it meets the limited-use liquid oil-fired subcategory identified at 63.9990(b)(3). Letter 2015-01-12, Region 1.

question: At our Michigan site we plan an epoxy dispersion process that makes a coating product; the final step filters the finished product to remove lumps and gels. If that filtering counts as a 'separation activity', we think the coatings manufacturing NESHAP would not apply and the miscellaneous organic chemical NESHAP might instead. How should we classify this process?
notes: Final filtering of a coating product is not a 'separation activity' under 63.8105, so HHHHH (miscellaneous coating manufacturing) applies if HAP-containing materials or HAP cleaning solvents are used, and FFFF does not (63.2435(b)(3) excludes coating manufacturing). Letter 2019-04-01, Region 5.

question: At our Colorado refinery, vapors from the truck loading rack in Plant 2 go to an enclosed vapor combustor. Is that combustor considered a flare under the petroleum refinery NESHAP, so that the refinery flare monitoring requirements apply to it?
notes: No. The vapor combustor does not meet the 63.641 definition of flare, so the 63.670 and 63.671 flare requirements do not apply; it must still be tested and operating parameters set and monitored to show compliance with the CC emission limits. Letter 2017-04-17, Region 8.

question: Our Virginia plant makes mica sheet insulation. On one line mica paper is fed from a roll through a coating line; on the other line the material is handled as sheets. Is either line a web coating line, and are the finished mica insulation products refractory products under the refractory NESHAP?
notes: Line 2 (roll-fed mica paper) is a web under 63.3300 and is subject to JJJJ; line 1 is not. The mica insulation products are not refractory products under 63.9824, so SSSSS does not apply. Letter 2016-07-12, Region 3.

question: At our natural gas transmission facility in New Mexico, a major source, the glycol dehydration unit is regulated under the gas transmission and storage NESHAP, with the still vent routed to a flare. The reboiler that heats the glycol burns field gas and its combustion exhaust goes straight to the atmosphere. Is the reboiler burner also a process heater under the boiler and process heater MACT?
notes: Yes. HHH covers only the still vent and flash tank emissions; the reboiler combustion chamber is a process heater under 63.7575 whose fuel is not regulated by another subpart and whose exhaust is uncontrolled, so DDDDD also applies. Letter 2016-03-21, Region 6.

question: Our Michigan steel plant, an area source, melts scrap in an electric arc furnace and turns the molten steel into shot and grit through a water atomization process rather than pouring it into sand molds. Trade groups call our product castings. Should we be regulated as an iron and steel foundry area source instead of as an electric arc furnace steelmaking area source?
notes: No. Without pouring molten metal into molds the facility is not an iron and steel foundry under the 63.10906 definition, so ZZZZZ (63.10880) does not apply; it remains subject to YYYYY (EAF steelmaking area sources) and NSPS AAa. Letter 2015-11-10, Region 5.

question: Our municipal utility in Louisiana has three natural-gas-fired electric generating boilers at an area source. They are permitted to burn fuel oil only during gas curtailment and for a limited number of test hours each year. Are these boilers subject to the area source boiler rule?
notes: Not subject to JJJJJJ as gas-fired boilers under 63.11195(e), provided the 63.11237 gas-fired boiler conditions are met (oil only during curtailment or supply interruption and limited testing hours), which should be locked in by permit limits. Letter 2015-07-28, Region 6.

question: Our Arkansas fiberboard plant runs a closed-loop gasification system: rotary gasifiers and a secondary combustion chamber burn wood residue, and most of the hot gas flows directly through the fiber dryers, which comply with the plywood and composite wood products NESHAP. Some hot gas bypasses the dryers to heat thermal oil. Since the dryers are covered by the wood products rule, is the whole gasification system exempt from the boiler and process heater MACT?
notes: No blanket exemption. Gas flowing directly through the dryers is part of the DDDD affected source (63.2232(b), 63.2292) and exempt from DDDDD, but gas used for indirect heat transfer to thermal oil makes the gasifiers and SCC process heaters under 63.7575 subject to DDDDD; 63.7491(h) does not cover the system. Letter 2014-08-11, Region 6.

question: Our Virginia sawmill plans to raise lumber production so that methanol emissions from the lumber dry kilns would exceed 10 tons per year, which would make us a major source of HAP. Would the plywood and composite wood products NESHAP then apply to us, and would the kilns become affected sources as soon as the revised permit reclassifying us is issued?
notes: Yes on both. Once potential methanol emissions exceed 10 tons per year the facility is a major source and is subject to DDDD from the date the revised permit is issued, at which point the lumber kilns are affected sources under 63.2232(b). Letter 2015-05-22, Region 3.

question: Our pharmaceutical plant in Ohio took federally enforceable limits on organic HAP before the chemical manufacturing area source rule took effect, so we are an area source. We now operate control devices, but even without them we would stay below the major source thresholds. Does the Title V permit requirement in that area source rule apply to us?
notes: No. Because the facility became an area source through operational limits before the rule's effective date and does not rely on control devices to stay below the major source thresholds, the Title V requirement in VVVVVV (63.11494) does not apply. Letter 2015-04-15, Region 5.
